# Incident Report: NetSupport RAT Infection — Host 10.11.26.183

**Capture window:** 2024-11-26 08:49:38 to 09:43:58 (local time, UTC+4) / 04:49:38–05:43:58 UTC
**Evidence:** `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap`, `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.txt`

## Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.11.26.183** |
| MAC address | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (confirmed via NBNS name registration and SMB2 session setup hostname field) |
| AD domain | NEMOTODES.HEALTH (DC: NEMOTODE-DC / NEMOTODES-DC, 10.11.26.3) |
| Logged-in user account | **oboomwald** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString, realm NEMOTODES.HEALTH) |

## Malware Family

**NetSupport RAT** (malicious repurposing of the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-access client).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** Suricata fired on this traffic with the following exact rule matches (not behavioral inference):
- `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`
- `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`
- `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin`
- `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Response`
- `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`

This is corroborated independently in the raw pcap: every C2 POST carries the literal HTTP header `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`, which is the genuine client's default UA string.

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control endpoint:**
- `194.180.191.64:443` — cleartext HTTP (not TLS, despite port 443) beacon target. Client repeatedly issues `POST http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm HTTP/1.1` with UA `NetSupport Manager/1.3`, roughly every 60 seconds from 08:50:45 through the end of the capture (09:43:29) — persistent RAT check-in/keepalive.
- `104.26.1.231:80` (Cloudflare-fronted) — `GET /location/loca.asp` to `geo.netsupportsoftware.com`, the NetSupport client's built-in geolocation lookup, performed once at first check-in (08:50:45).

**Malicious/suspicious domains (resolved and contacted by the victim):**
- `modandcrackedapk.com` → resolved to `193.42.38.139`; DNS lookup at 08:50:14, followed by a TLS session to 193.42.38.139 with SNI `modandcrackedapk.com` at 08:50:40. Flagged by Suricata (`ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup` / `...in TLS SNI`).
- `classicgrand.com` → resolved to `213.246.109.5`; TLS SNI contact at 08:50:11.
- `confirmsubscription.com` → resolved to `52.8.34.0`; TLS SNI contact at 08:50:14.
- `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` — legitimate NetSupport-owned domain used by the implant for its geolocation check.

These three sites (`classicgrand.com` → `confirmsubscription.com` → `modandcrackedapk.com`) were visited in immediate succession about 30 seconds before the first NetSupport RAT beacon fired, consistent with a fake "cracked APK / software download" redirect chain used to drop the RAT. All three sessions are TLS-encrypted with no decryption keys available in this evidence set, so the exact landing-page content and dropper delivery mechanism (e.g., the specific installer file) could not be recovered from the pcap.

**Malicious URL:**
- `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` — the sole URI used for all NetSupport C2 POST traffic.

**Transferred file names / hashes:**
- None recoverable. No plaintext HTTP object matching an executable/script extension (.exe/.dll/.zip/.msi/.ps1/.hta) was found via `tshark --export-objects`, and the delivery-chain sessions to classicgrand.com/confirmsubscription.com/modandcrackedapk.com were TLS-encrypted without available keys. No SHA256 can be stated from this evidence.

## Notes on other alerts (assessed as unrelated noise)

The alerts file also lists SMB/NTLM anomaly signatures (`GPL NETBIOS SMB Session Setup NTMLSSP unicode asn1 overflow attempt`, `SMB_COM_TRANSACTION Max Data Count of 0 DOS Attempt`, EFSR activity, SMBv1 usage) against the internal domain controller 10.11.26.3. Packet-level review shows this traffic is routine AD/GPO activity (SYSVOL group-policy file reads, DRSUAPI name lookups, NetServerEnum2 browsing) from the workstation to its DC — these are known false-positive-prone legacy signatures on normal domain-joined SMB/NTLM traffic and are not part of the NetSupport RAT infection chain.

## Summary

DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (10.11.26.183, MAC d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b), logged in as domain user `oboomwald` on NEMOTODES.HEALTH, browsed through a redirect chain (classicgrand.com → confirmsubscription.com → modandcrackedapk.com) around 08:50:11–08:50:40, then at 08:50:45 began beaconing to NetSupport RAT C2 at 194.180.191.64:443 (`POST /fakeurl.htm`, UA `NetSupport Manager/1.3`), confirmed via multiple ETPRO/ET Suricata signature hits, and continued that check-in every ~60 seconds for the remainder of the capture.
